chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan from 'Amr ibn Sa'id from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from 'Ammar ibn Musa from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about the vineyard (vines), when is it permissible to sell them? He said: When they form knots and become woody stems.
ai.seo_question: When is it permissible to sell grapevines according to Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the criterion for the permissibility of selling grapevines is defined by the development of 'urug' (woody stems), distinguishing mature, stable plants from mere young shoots. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on ensuring the subject matter of sale is sufficiently established and not merely speculative, aligning with the principles of *bay'* (sale) in Islamic commercial law. The hadith underscores the importance of physical maturity as a condition for valid ownership transfer in agricultural transactions.
